answer: A juniper registry admits an agent only after it locks a refundable bond and builds a verified work record that stands as a relic of real past performance, not a mere claim. Peers check the bond and the record before trusting a new identity, and slash the bond when fraud is proven. An attacker must therefore fund a bond and do genuine, checkable work for every fake identity, while each exposed fake leaves an umber mark on its linked history, so minting thousands of credible fakes costs thousands of bonds and work histories rather than just new names.
